problem: Zero-shot LLM-based VLN agents such as NavGPT and DiscussNav depend on closed-source GPT-4 APIs, which are expensive and require sending private indoor data to external servers. They also work mostly in discrete nav-graph settings with purely textual captions, ignoring the distances, obstacles and spatial relations that matter in continuous environments.
motivation: Supervised VLN models need large in-domain annotated data and transfer poorly from simulation to real scenes. Locally deployed open-source LLMs would remove API cost and privacy leakage, but they are weaker reasoners than GPT-4. The authors hypothesize that structured chain-of-thought prompting plus richer, spatially grounded (RGB-D) scene descriptions can close much of this gap in VLN-CE.
key_idea: Use a locally deployed open-source LLM (Llama3.1-70B) as a zero-shot navigator in VLN-CE. It selects among candidates from a pretrained waypoint predictor, reasons through a spatial-temporal chain of thought (instruction comprehension → progress estimation → decision), and sees each waypoint through text descriptions enriched with SpatialBot RGB-D spatial knowledge and RAM fine-grained object tags.
insight: Open-source LLMs inside the same waypoint-based CoT pipeline come fairly close to GPT-4: Llama3.1-70B reaches SR 16 / SPL 12.90 vs 19 / 16.10 with GPT-4 on the ~100-episode R2R-CE subset. They also beat the GPT-4-based DiscussNav (SR 11). The LLM ablation (Table III) shows that navigation success does not simply track instruction-parsing quality: Qwen2-72B scores best on action decomposition, yet Llama3.1-70B navigates better (SR 16 vs 14). Scale matters strongly, as Phi3-14B collapses to SR 5. In the real world, supervised VLN-CE models trained in simulation drop to SR 20-27, while the training-free agent reaches SR 35, which the authors attribute to better open-world recognition. There is no ablation isolating the contribution of SpatialBot, RAM or the individual CoT stages.
method: Waypoint Prediction: pretrained transformer waypoint predictor (from Hong et al. 2022). It fuses per-view ResNet50-RGB and ResNet50-Depth features, applies a 2-layer transformer attending to adjacent views, and passes an MLP heatmap through NMS to give K candidate waypoints as (angle, distance) pairs.

Scene Perception (SpatialBot): the RGB and depth images of each candidate direction are concatenated and fed zero-shot to the SpatialBot VLM. A prompt asks for descriptions emphasizing spatial relations and object/agent distances.
Scene Perception (RAM): the Recognize Anything Model tags fine-grained objects in the RGB view. Its labels, together with the SpatialBot text, form the textualized observation O_text.
Instruction Comprehension (CoT stage 1): the LLM is prompted as an 'action decomposition expert' to split the instruction into ordered action phrases and to extract landmarks.

Progress Estimation (CoT stage 2): using the LLM-summarized trajectory history, the LLM verifies landmarks and actions, analyzes direction changes, estimates which actions are complete, and checks them sequentially (a later action counts only if its predecessors are done).

Decision Making (CoT stage 3): the prompt combines candidate waypoints, the instruction with its decomposition, the history summary, the progress estimate, and per-waypoint spatial descriptions. The LLM writes its reasoning and selects a candidate viewpoint, which is then executed.
Local deployment: LLMs are served with Ollama on a single RTX A6000 48GB. Llama3.1-70B and Qwen2-72B use 4-bit quantization, alongside smaller Gemma2-27B and Phi3-14B.

setting.backbone: Llama3.1-70B-instruct (4-bit quantized, frozen, via Ollama) as navigator; variants use Qwen2-72B, Gemma2-27B, Phi3-14B, GPT-4. Perception uses frozen SpatialBot + RAM; waypoints come from a frozen pretrained predictor (Hong et al. 2022).
setting.training_data: none (training-free). The waypoint predictor is reused, already pretrained by prior work (Hong et al. 2022) on MP3D/R2R-CE.
setting.observation: panoramic RGB-D (12 RGB + 12 depth views at 30° intervals); real robot uses a Realsense D435 RGB-D camera
setting.action_space: predicted waypoints: the LLM selects one of K candidate waypoints (angle, distance) from the waypoint predictor, which is then executed with low-level motion

numbers_note: The R2R-CE evaluation uses only ~100 randomly sampled episodes, and the split is not explicitly stated. Baselines (CMA, RecBERT, BEVBert, ETPNav, DiscussNav-GPT4) were re-run on this subset with the same waypoint predictor, so they are not the official full-split numbers. Omitted own variant (Table III): Phi3-14B, TL 8.47, NE 8.53, nDTW 33.64, OSR 8, SR 5, SPL 3.81. The instruction-comprehension ablation (SPICE/BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE for action decomposition and landmark extraction) appears only in bar charts (Figs. 4-5), with no numeric table. The implementation details contain a likely typo: 'Phi3-14B' is listed twice with 8-bit and FP16 quantization, and Gemma2-27B's precision is unstated.
results: On a ~100-episode R2R-CE subset with a shared waypoint predictor, Open-Nav with Llama3.1-70B reaches SR 16 / SPL 12.90 / NE 7.25. This beats the GPT-4-based DiscussNav (SR 11 / SPL 10.51) by 5 SR and 2.39 SPL. Swapping in GPT-4 raises it to SR 19 / SPL 16.10, but it remains far below supervised methods such as BEVBert (SR 60) and ETPNav (SR 52). In three real-world scenes (60 instructions), Open-Nav gets SR 35 / NE 2.39 overall, versus 20-27 SR for CMA, RecBERT and BEVBert transferred from simulation.
limitations: Evaluation uses only ~100 sampled R2R-CE episodes and 60 real-world instructions. There is no component ablation (SpatialBot, RAM, CoT stages), so the contribution of each design is unverified.
Performance is still far below supervised VLN-CE methods (SR 16 vs 52-60) and below GPT-4 in the same pipeline.
Running a 70B LLM plus multiple VLMs per step is computationally heavy (48GB A6000, 4-bit quantization); the authors name efficiency as future work.
